title: The world will kiss your forehead while it poisons your soul.
paragraphs: The world will kiss your forehead while it poisons your soul.

Not always persecution.
Not always pain.
Sometimes it is applause.
Comfort.
Money.
Attention.
The slow addiction of being admired without being holy.
Scripture does not stutter: “Do not love the world or the things in the world” (1 John 2:15).

John is not saying trees are evil. Work is evil. Beauty is evil. He is warning us about a system that trains the heart to live without God. A world that celebrates lust, baptizes pride, and calls greed “success.” A world that says, “Follow your heart,” even when your heart is running from Christ.
And here is the scary part:

You can look clean in church…
and still be in love with the world.

You can sing worship on Sunday…
but crave validation, vanity, and secret compromise by Monday.

The danger of loving the world is not just that it makes you sin.
It makes you forget what you were made for.
Because “the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever” (1 John 2:17).

Everything this world sells has an expiration date.
The body fades.
Trends die.
Riches shift.
Fame turns on you.
Pleasure evaporates.

Christ did not die so you could be slightly religious and deeply worldly. He died to rescue you from empty desires, forgive your sin, break the chains of idols, and give you a heart that loves the Father more than the passing glitter of this age. That is the Gospel: we were wandering, craving lesser things, but Jesus came full of grace and truth to save sinners and bring us home.

What do you fear losing more than you fear grieving God?
What do you run to for identity, comfort, or worth?
What has your affection that belongs to Jesus?

Repentance is not misery.
It is mercy.

Turn back.
The Father is not calling you just to leave the world.
He is calling you to Himself.
And when Christ becomes your treasure, the world loses its spell.
